record.paper_title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let b(t,x)=b_t(x):(0,T)×R^d→R^d be a bounded possibly nonautonomous Borel velocity field, and consider the continuity equation ∂_t w_t + ∇·(b_t w_t)=0. Which assumptions on b ensure existence and uniqueness of nonnegative solutions in L^∞([0,T]; L^1(R^d) ∩ L^∞(R^d))?

evidence.quote: Here b(t, x) = bt(x) : (0, T) × R^d → R^d is a possibly nonautonomous Borel velocity field in R^d.
The main question is: which assumptions on b ensure that (1.1) has existence and uniqueness in L∞+[0, T];L1 ∩ L∞(Rd)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T>0$ and let $b:(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$, written $b(t,x)=b_t(x)$, be a bounded Borel measurable (possibly nonautonomous) vector field. Consider the linear continuity equation
$$\partial_t w_t + \nabla\cdot(b_t\, w_t) = 0 \quad \text{in } (0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d,$$
understood in the distributional sense, with initial data $w_0\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$, $w_0\geq 0$. Identify minimal structural conditions on $b$ (e.g., weak differentiability, bounds on the divergence, modulus of continuity, etc.) that guarantee existence and uniqueness of a nonnegative distributional solution
$$w\in L^\infty\bigl([0,T];\, L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)\bigr).$$
Characterize, as broadly as possible, the class of bounded Borel vector fields $b$ for which this well-posedness holds.
artifact.category_tag: Continuity equation with weakly differentiable vector fields
artifact.status_search_result: Well-posedness is known under various structural hypotheses: the DiPerna–Lions theory (Sobolev $W^{1,1}_{\rm loc}$ vector fields with bounded divergence), Ambrosio's extension to $BV_{\rm loc}$ vector fields with bounded divergence, and further refinements (nearly incompressible $BV$, suitable moduli of continuity, SBD, etc.). However, identifying the sharpest/most general assumptions on a merely bounded Borel vector field guaranteeing existence and uniqueness in $L^\infty([0,T];L^1\cap L^\infty)$ remains open; counterexamples (e.g., by Depauw, Alberti–Bianchini–Crippa, Bruè–Colombo–De Lellis) show non-uniqueness can occur outside these classes, but a complete characterization is not known.

status_evidence.title: Continuity equations and ODE flows with non-smooth velocity (Ambrosio)
status_evidence.snippet: Even for bounded and divergence-free vector fields, well-posedness of continuity equations is a nontrivial problem, since oscillations might lead to loss of uniqueness.
status_evidence.claim: The general well-posedness problem for bounded Borel vector fields is acknowledged as nontrivial and not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Well posedness of ODE's and continuity equations with nonsmooth vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews many aspects of the well-posedness theory for the Cauchy problem for the continuity and transport equations; covers many classes of vector fields.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results cover Sobolev and BV classes; the general problem continues to be investigated.

status_evidence.title: Some new well-posedness results for continuity and transport equations
status_evidence.snippet: New well-posedness results beyond Sobolev/BV settings.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues to extend the class of admissible vector fields.
